key_insight: Training report-generation models to align image-patch attention with pathologists’ own viewing patterns improves prostate histopathology reporting and makes model explanations more clinically meaningful.
clinical_relevance: This could help generate more accurate, visually grounded pathology reports and support downstream prostate cancer workflows such as report drafting and question answering.
method: Collected a multimodal dataset of 121 prostate whole-slide images with synchronized pathologist viewport trajectories, cursor movements, and verbal descriptions across five clinically relevant components.
Fine-tuned two report-generation models using an attention-alignment loss to match model attention over image patches to pathologist attention distributions.
Evaluated the approach on prostate cancer report generation and visual question answering with models using different internal attention mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average improvements of 10.9% on NLP-based metrics and 19.3% accuracy across five clinically relevant report components, with inference-time attention maps more closely matching pathologist attention.
watch_item: The dataset is relatively small and task-specific, so broader validation is needed before assuming the same gains will generalize across institutions, scanners, and pathology tasks.
paper_title: Pathologist Attention-Aligned Report Generation for Prostate Histopathology
